reason: GetInput has no `required` option; it returns (value, found) and the caller decides. Changing the signature would break the public API.
GetInput always trims and has no options parameter (public API).
GetBoolInput returns false for an invalid value where JS throws a TypeError; Go has no error return (public API).
GetBoolInput returns false for an unset input where JS throws a TypeError; Go has no error return (public API).
Group takes a func() and returns a deprecated no-op func(); JS group is generic and resolves to the callback's result. Returning the result would change the public signature.

JS prints '::error ::m' (a stray space) when the properties object has keys whose values are all empty. Go's AnnotationProperties is a struct whose zero value cannot be told apart from 'no properties', so it prints '::error::m'. The runner parses both identically.
Same as 'error with empty title': JS prints a stray space for a properties object with only unknown keys; the Go struct has no such notion (public API). The runner parses both identically.

Deliberate: JS builds '<dir>:undefined' (the text 'undefined') when PATH is unset. Go sets PATH to '<dir>' alone: a literal 'undefined' entry is a relative directory name, and a trailing separator would mean the current directory.
Same as 'addPath without PATH' (the add-path command is printed identically; only the resulting PATH differs).
